vignette: 69-year-old man with CCS class IV stable angina despite maximally tolerated metoprolol, amlodipine, isosorbide mononitrate, and ranolazine. Angiography reviewed by interventional cardiology and cardiac surgery shows diffuse distal disease not amenable to angioplasty, stenting, atherectomy, or bypass. LVEF is 40%. PET perfusion-metabolism imaging shows viable ischemic myocardium in the inferolateral wall that cannot be revascularized by direct coronary intervention. He has no arrhythmias, heart failure decompensation, or recent infarction. The procedure uses a laser FDA approved for transmyocardial revascularization. The cardiothoracic surgeon is trained in TMR, and the hospital documents that all ancillary personnel (physicians, nurses, operating room staff, technicians) are trained in the procedure and equipment. The hospital has a dedicated cardiac care unit with the necessary diagnostic and support services and conforms to ANSI Z136.3 laser safety standards.
rationale_note: CCS IV refractory to maximal therapy, diffuse non-revascularizable disease, EF 40%, PET viability, stable.

vignette: 72-year-old woman with CCS class III angina that became unstable 3 weeks ago; she was hospitalized, treated, and has been clinically stable for 2 weeks on maximally tolerated antianginal therapy, but angina persists. Her LVEF is exactly 25% by echocardiography. Angiography shows diffuse small-vessel disease not amenable to angioplasty, stenting, atherectomy, or bypass. Dobutamine stress echocardiography demonstrates viable ischemic myocardium in the anterior wall that cannot be revascularized by direct coronary intervention. The procedure uses a laser FDA approved for transmyocardial revascularization. The cardiothoracic surgeon is trained in TMR, and the hospital documents that all ancillary personnel (physicians, nurses, operating room staff, technicians) are trained in the procedure and equipment. The hospital has a dedicated cardiac care unit with the necessary diagnostic and support services and conforms to ANSI Z136.3 laser safety standards.
rationale_note: Boundary: EF exactly 25%; CCS III unstable angina (stable or unstable allowed) after stabilization.

vignette: 82-year-old man with diabetes and two prior coronary bypass operations, now with occluded grafts and native vessels unsuitable for further bypass, angioplasty, stenting, or atherectomy. He has CCS class IV angina despite maximum safe doses of beta blocker, nitrate, calcium channel blocker, and ranolazine. LVEF is 45%. Nuclear viability imaging shows viable ischemic myocardium in the lateral wall not capable of direct revascularization. He is clinically stable. The procedure uses a laser FDA approved for transmyocardial revascularization. The cardiothoracic surgeon is trained in TMR, and the hospital documents that all ancillary personnel (physicians, nurses, operating room staff, technicians) are trained in the procedure and equipment. The hospital has a dedicated cardiac care unit with the necessary diagnostic and support services and conforms to ANSI Z136.3 laser safety standards.
rationale_note: Two prior CABGs with failed grafts, age 82, diabetes are not exclusions.
